issues.legal_issue: A body for whose benefit land is acquired may participate in compensation proceedings and must receive notice of the proceedings.
material_facts: The land was acquired for a statutory housing board, which was responsible for paying the compensation.
The board was not given notice of the compensation proceedings before either the acquisition officer or the reference tribunal.
The board had not appeared in those proceedings to present evidence.
issues.conclusion: A local authority or company for whose benefit land is acquired may appear and adduce evidence on compensation before the Collector and the reference court. That right includes adequate notice of when compensation will be determined.
issues.legal_principle: Section 50(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 grants the right to appear and adduce evidence, subject to its proviso barring a demand for a reference under Section 18. The notice requirement is implicit in that right. Neelgangabai v. State of Karnataka and Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti v. Ashok Singhal support the consequence of denying the beneficiary body an opportunity to participate; the Court also considered Union of India v. Sher Singh and Union of India v. Kolluni Ramaiah.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: An authority is determining compensation for land acquired for another body’s benefit.
predicates.beneficiary_body_pays_compensation: The body for whose benefit the land is acquired is responsible for paying the compensation.
predicates.beneficiary_body_can_present_evidence: The body for whose benefit the land is acquired seeks to present evidence relevant to compensation.

issues.definition: When compensation is being determined for land acquired for a body that pays for it and may present relevant evidence, that body is entitled to notice and an opportunity to present evidence.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary body denied its opportunity to participate may seek judicial review of a compensation determination, subject to the limits on review.
material_facts: The board received no notice from the acquisition officer or the reference tribunal and did not participate at either stage.
The board challenged the High Court’s enhancement of compensation, which increased the amount it would have to pay.
The Court directed that the board be joined in the landowners’ appeals and that those appeals be reheard.
issues.conclusion: A beneficiary body may invoke Article 226 when lack of notice denies its Section 50(2) participation right. If it received notice, judicial review is confined to grounds on which such review is available; a body that failed to participate despite notice ordinarily has no grievance, subject to exceptional grounds such as mala fides or perversity.
issues.legal_principle: Section 50(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 confers a participation right, and Article 226 provides judicial review when that right is denied. The proviso to Section 50(2) bars a demand for a reference under Section 18, but does not bar judicial review. Neelgangabai v. State of Karnataka is relied on for relief where failure to give notice deprived the beneficiary body of an opportunity to be heard. The Court distinguishes the beneficiary body’s limited review rights from the broader appeal rights of parties to the proceedings.

rule.if: compensation_determination_challenge and beneficiary_body_aggrieved and (no_notice_prevented_participation or (notice_received and participated and (opportunity_to_present_evidence_denied or evidence_not_considered or malafides)) or (notice_received and did_not_participate and (malafides or perversity)))

predicates.compensation_determination_challenge: A body challenges a determination of compensation for land acquired for its benefit.
predicates.beneficiary_body_aggrieved: The body for whose benefit the land was acquired is adversely affected by the compensation determination.
predicates.no_notice_prevented_participation: The decision-maker did not notify the beneficiary body, and the body consequently could not participate.
predicates.notice_received: The beneficiary body was notified of the compensation proceedings.
predicates.participated: The beneficiary body appeared in the proceedings.
predicates.opportunity_to_present_evidence_denied: The beneficiary body appeared but was not allowed an opportunity to present relevant evidence.
predicates.evidence_not_considered: The decision-maker did not consider evidence presented by the beneficiary body.
predicates.malafides: The beneficiary body alleges that the compensation determination was made in bad faith.
predicates.did_not_participate: The beneficiary body did not appear in the proceedings despite being notified.
predicates.perversity: The compensation determination is alleged to be perverse.

issues.definition: A body adversely affected by a compensation determination may seek judicial review if it was prevented from participating by lack of notice, if its participation was unfairly restricted, or, despite receiving notice and not appearing, if the determination was tainted by bad faith or perversity.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary local authority is a proper party in proceedings on a reference concerning compensation.
material_facts: The landowners sought references against the acquisition officer’s compensation award.
The board was not joined in the proceedings before the reference tribunal.
The board was the body responsible for paying compensation and was entitled to present evidence on its determination.
issues.conclusion: A local authority for whose benefit land is acquired is a proper party and is entitled to be impleaded in proceedings before the reference court, where it may defend the acquisition officer’s award, oppose an increase in compensation, and adduce evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Section 50(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 gives the beneficiary body the right to appear and adduce evidence before the reference court. Applying the necessary-party and proper-party distinction in Udit Narain Singh Malpaharia v. Additional Member, Board of Revenue, the Court held the local authority to be a proper party. The proviso to Section 50(2) prevents it from demanding a reference under Section 18, but does not prevent it from participating in a reference sought by a person interested in the land.

predicates.compensation_reference_proceeding: A court is hearing a reference concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.land_acquired_for_local_authority: The land was acquired for the benefit of a local authority.
predicates.local_authority_pays_compensation: The local authority is responsible for paying the compensation.

issues.definition: When a court hears a compensation reference concerning land acquired for a local authority that pays the compensation, the authority is entitled to be joined.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary local authority must be joined and notified in an appeal by a landowner seeking increased compensation.
material_facts: The landowners appealed seeking an increase in the compensation awarded by the reference tribunal.
The board was responsible for paying the compensation but had not been joined in those appeals.
The board had not been notified of the earlier compensation proceedings.
issues.conclusion: In an appeal by a person interested in the land seeking enhancement of compensation, the beneficiary local authority must be impleaded and served notice so that it can defend the reference court’s award and oppose enhancement. The Court directed that the board be joined in the landowners’ appeals and remitted those appeals for decision after hearing the parties.
issues.legal_principle: Section 50(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 recognizes the beneficiary body’s interest in compensation and its right to adduce evidence. The Court relied on the principles applied in Neelgangabai v. State of Karnataka, Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti v. Ashok Singhal, and Union of India v. Sher Singh in recognizing the beneficiary body’s entitlement to participate. The ruling applies equally to appeals in the High Court and the Supreme Court; finally concluded matters are not reopened.

rule.if: landowner_compensation_appeal and appeal_seeks_higher_compensation and land_acquired_for_local_authority and local_authority_pays_compensation

predicates.landowner_compensation_appeal: A person interested in the acquired land appeals against a compensation determination.
predicates.appeal_seeks_higher_compensation: The appeal seeks to increase the compensation awarded by the reference court.
predicates.land_acquired_for_local_authority: The land was acquired for the benefit of a local authority.
predicates.local_authority_pays_compensation: The local authority is responsible for paying the compensation.

issues.definition: When a landowner appeals seeking increased compensation for land acquired for a local authority that pays for it, the authority must be joined and notified.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary local authority may appeal an enhanced compensation award when the government does not appeal, but it must obtain leave.
material_facts: The reference tribunal had determined compensation for land acquired for the board.
The board could be prejudicially affected if the reference court enhanced the compensation.
The Court considered the case in which the government does not appeal an enhancement made by the reference court.
issues.conclusion: If the reference court enhances compensation and the government does not appeal, a local authority adversely affected by the enhancement may appeal to the High Court after obtaining leave of the court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the proviso to Section 50(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 bars a beneficiary local authority from demanding a reference under Section 18 but does not eliminate the appeal remedy against an enhanced award of the reference court, subject to leave. Union of India v. Sher Singh and Union of India v. Kolluni Ramaiah were considered in addressing the beneficiary body’s ability to challenge an adverse determination. The Court treated the right of appeal as a legal remedy distinct from the prohibited demand for a reference.

rule.if: reference_court_enhanced_compensation and local_authority_adversely_affected and government_did_not_appeal and local_authority_obtains_leave

predicates.reference_court_enhanced_compensation: The reference court increased the compensation awarded for acquired land.
predicates.local_authority_adversely_affected: The increased compensation adversely affects the local authority for whose benefit the land was acquired.
predicates.government_did_not_appeal: The government did not appeal the reference court’s enhancement.
predicates.local_authority_obtains_leave: The local authority obtained the appellate court’s permission to appeal.

issues.definition: A local authority adversely affected by an enhancement may appeal when the government has not appealed, provided the authority obtains leave.

issues.legal_issue: A company for whose benefit land is acquired has the same participation and related procedural rights as a local authority.
material_facts: The judgment considered acquisitions made for a company as well as acquisitions made for a local authority.
The acquiring body is responsible for the compensation and may present evidence concerning its amount.
issues.conclusion: The rights and procedural rules stated for a local authority under Section 50(2) apply equally to a company for whose benefit land is acquired.
issues.legal_principle: Section 50(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 expressly applies to a local authority or company. The Court relied on Himalayan Tiles & Marbles (P) Ltd. v. Francis Victor Countinho for the company’s ability to participate in determining compensation, while explaining that the relevant basis is Section 50(2), rather than treating the company as a person entitled to demand a reference under Section 18.

predicates.land_acquired_for_company: The land was acquired for the benefit of a company.
predicates.company_pays_compensation: The company for whose benefit the land was acquired is responsible for paying the compensation.

issues.definition: A company that benefits from the acquisition and pays the compensation has the same participation rights as a local authority.

issues.legal_issue: A compensation determination that has become finally concluded is not reopened under the procedural rules stated for beneficiary bodies.
material_facts: The Court recognized the beneficiary body’s rights to notice, participation, and remedies in compensation proceedings.
The Court expressly preserved matters that had already been finally concluded.
issues.conclusion: Matters that stand finally concluded are not reopened.
issues.legal_principle: The Court expressly limited its conclusions concerning the rights of local authorities and companies by preserving the finality of matters already concluded.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: A proceeding concerns compensation for acquired land.
predicates.determination_finally_concluded: The determination has become finally concluded.

issues.definition: In a compensation case concerning acquired land, a determination that is finally concluded is not reopened.
